The test image shows a soybean **stem split lengthwise** revealing dark brown/black internal pith and vascular discoloration. This is a stem symptom.

Top candidates from the stem class list: Brown_Stem_Rot, Charcoal_Rot, Phytophthora, Fusarium, Anthracnose, White_Mold, Rhizoctonia, Tobacco_Streak_Virus.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with the strongest candidates.
This Brown_Stem_Rot reference shows a split stem with mostly white pith and only slight browning. The test image has much more extensive, dark brown-black discoloration. Let me check Charcoal_Rot.
This shows external charcoal rot symptoms (gray streaking). Let me check the other charcoal rot stem reference and then Phytophthora.
Charcoal rot shows external microsclerotia specks and lighter internal pith. The test image has heavily darkened internal pith. Let me check Phytophthora.
Phytophthora shows external dark brown stem discoloration, not a split stem. Let me check Fusarium and Anthracnose stems.
Fusarium doesn't match. Let me check Anthracnose stem and White_Mold stem.
White Mold shows bleached stem with sclerotia, not matching. Let me use my last view on Charcoal_Rot whole plant to compare the overall plant context.

Now I have all 8 views used across 8 different classes. Let me synthesize.

**Test image analysis**: A soybean stem split lengthwise revealing extensive dark brown/black internal pith discoloration. The plant is still green and actively growing, with healthy-looking green leaves surrounding the stem.

**Key differentiators**:
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Classic diagnostic is "browning of pith and vascular tissue visible when stems are split lengthwise" while "externally infected stems appear healthy." The green plant with an internally brown stem is the hallmark.
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Shows microsclerotia (distinct small black specks) giving a "charcoal-sprinkled" appearance, typically on wilting/stressed plants. The references showed gray external streaking.
- Other stem diseases (Phytophthora, White_Mold, Anthracnose, Fusarium) showed distinctly different patterns (external lesions, white mold growth, or root-focused symptoms).

The combination of (1) externally healthy green plant, (2) stem split lengthwise, and (3) extensive brown pith discoloration is the textbook diagnostic for Brown Stem Rot. The KB confirms: "Healthy stems have white pith, while BSR-infected stems have brown pith."
